Use a cascaded pipeline: exact/perceptual hashes for known content, cheap modality-specific models for broad triage, expensive multimodal analysis for ambiguous cases, and trained human review for high-impact uncertainty. Moderation decisions must bind to a policy version and distinguish removal, reduced distribution, labeling, and escalation.

Fuse text, image, audio, temporal context, and behavior where permitted. A hash match can be high precision for a known item but is not a general misinformation detector; semantic classifiers also need context and uncertainty. Propagate decisions consistently across copies while preserving appealability and evidence.

Set thresholds from false-positive/negative costs and review capacity. Evaluate languages, dialects, minority contexts, and adversarial edits separately; aggregate accuracy can hide serious failures. Maintain an appeal workflow, reviewer quality audits, and sampled checks of automatically cleared content. Queue outages should trigger a defined distribution/review policy. New policy and model releases need shadow tests and rollback because disagreement may reflect policy ambiguity rather than a model bug.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For review capacity C, choose thresholds jointly with the expected arrival rate into each queue. A model with better aggregate accuracy can still overload reviewers or miss a rare severe category. Measure policy-specific precision/recall, turnaround time, appeal overturns, and subgroup slices, preserving evidence and policy versions so disagreements can be audited.
